answer: Lindell threshold ECDSA keeps the signing key split between two parties who multiply their shares inside Paillier ciphertexts, so the umber of the secret never appears in the clear. Each party proves its pulse is well-formed before the joint signature is released, which blocks a Sybil from registering many weak identities and combining them. The final signature looks ordinary, but behind it a glacier of cold key material stayed split the whole time.
